about.title: Our Historical Foundation
about.description: During the time of the Mongol Empire, the “Gerege” was a diplomatic passport issued to emissaries and envoys. It granted them safe passage, food, horses, lodging, and guides across the vast territory of the empire. It was the world’s first form of a universal travel token—unparalleled in any other civilization, even the Roman Empire. The holder of a Gerege traveled freely and received honorable hospitality, symbolizing power, trust, and international authority.

about.title: Modern Rebirth – The Gerege Tourist Passport
about.description: The Gerege Tourist Passport is a contemporary version of this historical legacy—reimagined for today’s travelers. Designed to promote Mongolia’s culture and history to international tourists, it combines educational value with real-world benefits: free access to 8 services, discounts at over 100 partner businesses, and contributions to charitable causes such as children’s welfare.

about.title: Safe, Simple, Smart, and Saving – The Four Pillars of the Gerege Tourist Passport
about.description:
These four keywords represent the core strengths of the Gerege Tourist Passport:

  • Safe: Officially registered and secure, your personal data is protected. The passport supports responsible and safe travel across Mongolia.
  • Simple: Easy to purchase, use, and redeem discounts. The experience is user-friendly and convenient for all travelers.
  • Smart: Enhanced with technology—QR codes, an online network of partners, and seamless integration to make your journey efficient and smooth.
  • Saving: Access discounts at over 100 establishments including hotels, restaurants, and attractions—helping you reduce travel costs without sacrificing quality.

The Gerege Tourist Passport is your trusted companion—bridging ancient Mongolian legacy with modern-day travel in a way that is educational, valuable, and inspiring.

NewsAndTips.title: NEWS
NewsAndTips.description: Here’s many things you can do in Ulaanbaatar for free and others

news.title: Khuvsgul Lake
news.description: Often referred to as the 'Switzerland of Mongolia,' Khuvsgul Lake boasts crystal-clear waters surrounded by majestic mountains and dense forests. It is a popular destination for nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts.

news.title: Orkhon Valley
news.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site, the Orkhon Valley is rich in history and culture. It features notable landmarks such as the Orkhon Waterfall, the ancient city of Kharkhorin, and the Erdene Zuu Monastery, offering a glimpse into Mongolia's past.

news.title: Gobi Three Beauties
news.description: Located in Umnugobi Province, this stunning natural area includes breathtaking attractions like Yolyn Am, the Dungenee Rock, and the Khongoryn Els sand dunes, showcasing the unique beauty of the Gobi Desert.

news.title: Khorgo and Terkhiin Tsagaan Lake
news.description: This region in Arkhangai Province features a volcanic crater, unique geological formations, and pristine freshwater lakes, making it an ideal spot for hiking and exploring nature.

news.title: Altai Tavan Bogd
news.description: Situated in western Mongolia, Altai Tavan Bogd is known for its majestic mountains, glacial rivers, and the rich cultural heritage of the nomadic Kazakh people, making it a stunning destination for adventure seekers.

news.title: Amarbayasgalant Monastery
news.description: As one of the largest and oldest monasteries in Mongolia, Amarbayasgalant is a remarkable architectural site that preserves cultural heritage and offers a serene atmosphere for visitors.

news.title: Uvs Lake
news.description: A UNESCO-listed area, the Uvs Lake Basin features a unique landscape that combines steppes, desert, and mountainous regions, providing diverse habitats for wildlife.

news.title: Khustain Nuruu
news.description: Home to the endangered Przewalski's horse, Khustain Nuruu is a protected area dedicated to the conservation and breeding of this rare species in its natural habitat.

news.title: Burkan Khaldun Mountain
news.description: Known as the birthplace of Genghis Khan, Burkan Khaldun Mountain is one of Mongolia's most sacred sites, rich in historical significance and natural beauty.

news.title: Ogii Lake
news.description: Located in Arkhangai Province, Ogii Lake is a picturesque destination ideal for fishing and birdwatching, featuring clear waters and a tranquil environment.
